statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 15% (low), Stress 40% (moderate), Confidence 88% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail stays in the low band, so the mapped state remains EA_ON. The basis is a third observed rejection of the session high rather than an absence of evidence: the Nasdaq-100 has held roughly 97 points below its 30,699.00 record for about an hour, NQ futures are some 82 points below 30,997.00, and neither the high nor the 30,496.43 low has extended. VIX at 14.33 is down 3.6% near the session low, 2-year and 10-year yields are effectively unchanged, and the tape is rotational rather than aligned, with the Dow down 0.4% and software weak against a strong semiconductor complex. The narrow danger window is placed on the 23 September US cash open and flash PMI cluster, the only forecast hour that reaches the caution band.
headline: The Nasdaq-100 has spent about an hour balanced between its 30,699.00 record high and the 30,496.43 session open, with a falling VIX and flat yields leaving no one-way structure in the tape.
body:
Tuesday's US cash session has now produced a third failure to extend, and that is what holds this assessment in the low Tail band. At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 is 30,601.53, up 0.39%, sitting 97 points under the 30,699.00 intraday record and 105 points above the 30,496.43 open, which is also the day's low. December NQ futures are 30,915.25, up 0.42%, 82 points under their 30,997.00 high. Both highs are unchanged from the previous hourly assessment, so the index has failed to extend while giving back roughly half of the move off the open. Mean reversion is working, and the session-extreme-holding and shallow-pullback conditions that the Tail score requires are absent.

Cross-asset evidence points the same way rather than aligning behind a single direction. VIX is 14.33, down 3.6% and close to its 14.29 session low. The 10-year yield is 4.974%, up about one basis point inside a 4.926 to 4.978 range, and the 2-year is 4.762%, essentially unchanged, so there is no rate impulse for equities to trend on. WTI is near 91.77 dollars and lower for a fifth consecutive session after Iran signalled a willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a de-escalating rather than escalating geopolitical direction, though President Trump's UN remarks that a deal is more likely after the November midterms leave the headline channel two-way. Breadth is rotational: the Dow is down 0.4% with financials the drag, the Russell 2000 is higher, semiconductors are firm for a sixth straight session with AMD passing a trillion dollars in market value, while software trades lower. Delayed Finviz context is only partially available this run, with futures and calendar sections missing, and its usable megacap section is split five up and three down with high dispersion, which corroborates rotation rather than index-level trend.

Stress is held at 40%, in the moderate band, reflecting an index at record levels, a 10-year yield pressing 5%, a five-session oil slide and live Middle East diplomacy, none of which currently translate into a pathological price path. Confidence is 88% because the price, volatility, rate and oil readings were all taken live within minutes of the cutoff and the near-term calendar has been confirmed against two independent sources.

The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail between 11% and 21%. The remaining US cash hours rise modestly to 18% through the power hour and the 20:00 UTC close, then fall through the thin overnight window to a floor of 11%. The profile rebuilds through the European session on Wednesday and peaks at 21% in the hour following the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC, which lands 15 minutes after the US cash open. That single hour is the only one to reach the caution band and carries the WATCH mapping; the danger window is drawn narrowly around that cluster, from 13:30 to 14:30 UTC, rather than across the whole session.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments, none of them revised with later information. Monday's late US session carried Tail in the elevated band at 28 to 33% under a trend-up mode, then stepped down to WATCH at 23% and into the low band at 14% as that session closed. The overnight and European hours held Tail between 11% and 13% in a normal mode. Tuesday's US open lifted Tail to 21% and WATCH for one hour on an opening push, after which the first rejection of the record high returned it to 17% and a mixed mode in the hour before this assessment.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside an 11 to 21% band, and only one forecast hour reaches the caution band. The remaining US cash hours rise modestly from 15% to 18% through the power hour and the 20:00 UTC close, then fall through the post-close and Asian hours to a floor of 11%. The profile rebuilds gradually through the European session on Wednesday and peaks at 21% with a WATCH mapping in the hour after the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC, which follows the US cash open by 15 minutes. It eases to 19% in the final hour on the assumption that post-event price discovery is orderly. Confidence decays from 88% to 68% across the horizon as the live evidence behind this assessment ages.

Neither extreme has extended for roughly an hour. VIX 14.33 (-3.6%), 10Y 4.974% (+1bp). Two-way midday balance keeps Tail in the low band.

forecast.analysis: Fed Barkin (non-voter) speaks and the US 2-year note auction settles in this hour. Both are checkpoints rather than Tail drivers. Tail edges up one point only because two scheduled items land together; a block would require the auction or the remarks to produce a rate move that equities then trend on without retracement.

US 2-Year Note auction at 17:00 UTC; watch the tail and 2Y reaction
Condition to watch: a yield jump that equities extend on without a pullback
Baseline assumption: orderly absorption, consistent with flat 2Y so far

forecast.analysis: Early-afternoon US trade, typically the session's quietest stretch. With no scheduled release in this hour, the conditional risk is a slow drift that quietly removes two-way trade ahead of the close. Tail stays in the low band unless the record high is reclaimed and held rather than rejected a third time.
drivers: No scheduled US release inside this hour
Invalidation: NDX reclaiming 30,699.00 and holding above it
Post-auction rate tone carried over from the previous hour
Oil weakness into a fifth session remains a supportive backdrop

forecast.analysis: Power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close. This is the session's structurally highest-risk stretch because index-level positioning concentrates here, and with the index near record territory a late one-way push is the realistic adverse path. Conditional only: no such structure is observed at the assessment cutoff.
drivers: Power hour: late-session continuation risk near record highs
Conditional trigger: acceptance above 30,699.00 late in the session
Quarter-end positioning flows can thin out counter-trend liquidity
Still below the block threshold; mapped state remains EA_ON

forecast.analysis: The 20:00 UTC cash close and settlement. Closing imbalances can produce a sharp final print, but that move is usually a single impulse rather than the sustained no-retracement path the Tail score measures. Stress stays moderate; Tail holds at the same level as the preceding hour.

Settlement impulses are typically one-off, not persistent trends
A record close would confirm strength but is not by itself a Tail event
Cash-session evidence quality begins to decline after the close

forecast.analysis: Post-close hour. Liquidity thins and NQ futures become the only continuous reference. Tail steps down because the concentrated closing flows are past and no scheduled catalyst follows. Residual risk is a headline gap in thin books rather than a trending price path.
drivers: Cash session closed; NQ futures are the continuous reference
No scheduled US macro release after the close
Thin-book headline gap risk replaces trend-continuation risk
Iran/Hormuz diplomacy remains the live two-way headline channel

forecast.analysis: Evening Globex. Volumes fall sharply and the tape normally reverts to range behaviour. The dominant mode shifts to normal on the assumption that no new catalyst arrives. Confidence declines gradually because live price-path evidence from the assessment cutoff is ageing.
drivers: Evening Globex: low volume, range-bound baseline expectation
No scheduled catalyst in this hour
Confidence decays as cutoff price-path evidence ages
Assumption to revisit: no overnight geopolitical headline

forecast.analysis: Late US evening ahead of the Asian handover. Historically the lowest-activity hour of the 24-hour cycle for NQ, and the conditional Tail path is correspondingly thin. Tail reaches its lowest forecast level here.
drivers: Lowest-activity hour of the NQ cycle; minimal trend capacity
Pre-Asia handover with no scheduled data
Lowest Tail level across the 24-hour forecast
Oil direction after five down sessions is the main overnight variable

forecast.analysis: Asian session opens. Japanese and Korean cash markets set the early tone, and semiconductor-complex sentiment there can feed back into NQ. Given the strong but rotational semi tape into the US cutoff, a modest positive handover is the base case, with range behaviour still assumed.
drivers: Asian cash open; Japan and Korea set the early tone
Semi-complex read-across after a sixth straight up day in US chips
Base case: range behaviour, no directional persistence
Watch for any Iran or oil headline landing in Asian hours

forecast.analysis: Asian morning. Cross-asset behaviour in this window is usually a continuation of the handover tone rather than an independent driver of index-level trend. Tail holds at its floor; Stress stays low-moderate on the assumption of an orderly session.
drivers: Asian morning: handover tone usually persists without new trend
No US scheduled data in this window
Assumption: orderly Asian session with no volatility shock
Yen and rates moves are the usual read-across channel

forecast.analysis: Asian midday into the lunch break. Tail ticks up a single point purely because the following hours begin to build toward the European handover, not because of any observed structure. Nothing in this window carries a scheduled catalyst.
drivers: Asian midday; activity dips through the lunch period
Very small upward drift toward the European handover
No scheduled catalyst; conditional reasoning only
Evidence freshness continues to decline

forecast.analysis: Asian afternoon. The session closes out with positioning ahead of Europe. Conditional risk remains low, and the assessment continues to assume the two-way behaviour observed at the cutoff carries into the new day rather than resolving into a trend.

Core assumption: two-way behaviour persists into the new day

drivers: Pre-European hour; overnight range usually firms here
No scheduled release in this window
Overnight range integrity is the condition to watch
Baseline remains range behaviour rather than trend

Overnight range test is the standard behaviour in this hour

European-led moves rarely drive persistent NQ trend
Semiconductor names in Europe give an early sector read

Semis firm against weaker software was the cutoff-day pattern

Risk profile builds gradually toward the 13:45 UTC PMI

forecast.analysis: The danger window opens at 13:30 UTC with the US cash open, and the S&P Global flash PMI lands at 13:45 UTC, 15 minutes later. That pairing of an opening auction with a high-impact release is the clearest scheduled cluster in the forecast horizon, so Tail and Stress both step up within this hour.

Opening auction paired with a high-impact print inside one hour
Danger window opens at 13:30 UTC (15:30 Berlin)

forecast.analysis: The highest-risk hour in the forecast: the first full hour after the flash PMI, inside the danger window, which closes at 14:30 UTC. The composite, manufacturing and services prints can repeatedly reverse direction as they are digested. Tail reaches the caution band here and the mapped state becomes WATCH.
drivers: First full hour after the 13:45 UTC flash PMI release
Three sub-indices can drive repeated direction changes

Peak forecast Tail at 21%; mapped state WATCH
Conditional: a failed retracement here would justify reassessment

forecast.analysis: Post-PMI digestion, one hour after the danger window closes. Under the applied method Tail is allowed to fall quickly once price discovery is orderly and retracements appear. The step down to 19% assumes that normal outcome; a persistent no-retracement path would instead keep it elevated.
drivers: Post-PMI digestion; orderly discovery is the base case
Tail falls quickly when retracements appear after an event
Mapped state returns to EA_ON at 19%
Invalidation: repeated extension after failed pullbacks
Last hour of the 24-hour forecast horizon
